subject: Computer Networking
title: How Online Gaming Stays Fast
description: A short lesson to help you apply How Online Gaming Stays Fast.

hook.text: In an online game, 100 players act simultaneously. Everyone sees the same world in real time. How?

buildup.text: Games use UDP for speed. They send tiny position updates dozens of times per second to a central server.

discovery.text: The server reconciles everyone's actions into one truth and sends the result back to all players.

twist.text: Lag gives some players an unfair advantage. That's why competitive games invest heavily in low-latency servers.

climax.text: Prediction algorithms guess where you'll move next, smoothing the experience even when packets arrive late.

punchline.text: Online gaming is a latency war disguised as fun.

quiz.question: Why do online games typically use UDP instead of TCP?
options: UDP's lower overhead reduces latency for real-time updates
UDP is more reliable than TCP

details.summary: Online games use UDP for speed, client-side prediction to mask latency, and server reconciliation to maintain consistency. The game client renders actions immediately while the server validates and corrects them.
details.whyItMatters: Online gaming pushes network performance to the extreme. The techniques used to hide latency are relevant to any real-time application needing instant responsiveness.
takeaways: Games use UDP for minimal latency over reliable delivery
Client-side prediction renders actions before server confirmation
Server reconciliation corrects discrepancies between client and server

faq.question: What is client-side prediction in gaming?
faq.answer: When you press a key, the game client immediately shows the result without waiting for the server. The server later confirms or corrects the action. If the server disagrees, the client rewinds and replays. This makes the game feel responsive despite network latency.

faq.question: Why is ping so important for online games?
faq.answer: Ping measures the round-trip time to the game server. Lower ping means less delay between your action and the server's response. High ping makes client-side prediction less accurate, causing rubber-banding and desyncs. Competitive gamers need under 30ms ping for fair play.
